title: Ines and the Veil
premise: Ulyana Delacroix, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has hidden his magic for seven years in Veymar, a city where spells are punishable by drowning. When a dying courier named Ines presses a bloodstained map into his hands and dies in his shop, Ulyana learns the king of Veymar is bound to an ancient entity called the Veil, which feeds on the city's outlawed magic to grow stronger. Hunted by the Veil's inquisitors, Ulyana gathers a ragtag found family—Ines's vengeful sister, a defector priest, and a child who can hear the map sing—and follows it to the drowned cathedral beneath the palace. There he discovers the original oath: his own order swore the king to the Veil to end a war, and only a swordspeaker can unbind it, at the cost of his own voice and magic. Ulyana breaks the oath, destroys the Veil, loses his power, and finds that the family he made along the way was worth more than the magic he surrendered.
about_author: Emrys Blackwood is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write about magic that costs something, and people who pay anyway.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Seven years of small charms, false names, and careful invisibility in Veymar's night market. When an inquisitor nearly catches him selling a luck-knot, we see how tightly he binds himself. Emotional beat: the loneliness of self-erasure.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A bleeding stranger stumbles into his shop at closing time, presses a folded map into his hands, and whispers 'the king is not the king' before dying on the floorboards. Ulyana hides the body and the map. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Map Sings
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The map hums with old swordspeech—a dialect only his order used. He realizes the dead man knew what he was. An inquisitorial sweep of the district forces him to flee with nothing but the map. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Ines
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The dead courier's sister, a dockworker with a smuggler's network, confronts the stranger her brother died reaching. She doesn't trust Ulyana but recognizes the map's seal—their grandmother's mark. She demands in. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: The Drowned Cathedral
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Following the map's first clue beneath the harbor, Ulyana and Ines find a flooded chapel where swordspeakers once trained—and evidence they didn't die out. They were purged, by royal decree, seven years ago. Emotional beat: betrayal by history.

chapters.title: Brother Cassian
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. A palace priest who has begun doubting the confessions he hears from the king's chamber—confessions in no human tongue. He seeks out rumors of a surviving swordspeaker. Emotional beat: faith cracking under weight.

chapters.title: The Child Who Hears It
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A street orphan named Pip can hear the map singing too, and the inquisitors have noticed children like Pip vanishing. Ines takes the child in; Ulyana objects until Pip repeats a phrase in perfect swordspeech. Emotional beat: family forming against will.

chapters.title: Seven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV (flashback). The purge: Ulyana's master ordered the students scattered and the great oath sealed, telling Ulyana that silence was the last duty. He ran instead of fighting. Emotional beat: shame revealed as the wound beneath his hiding.

chapters.title: Audience with the Crown
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Cassian arranges a forged invitation that lets Ulyana enter the palace as a charm-seller. From behind a screen, Ulyana sees the king—and the shadow moving beneath his skin like water. Emotional beat: horror confirmed.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing Him
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The Veil senses a swordspeaker in the palace and turns the city's inquisitors loose. A chase through the merchant quarter; Ines is wounded covering their escape. Emotional beat: the cost of being seen.

chapters.title: Triage and Truths
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Tending Ines's wound with forbidden healing magic, Ulyana confesses everything: the order, the oath, his flight. Ines, feverish, tells him about her brother's letters—he'd been investigating the disappearances for months. Emotional beat: intimacy through honesty.

chapters.title: The Defector's Bargain
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Cassian brings stolen liturgical records showing the binding rite requires a swordspeaker's voice spoken inside the old cathedral, on the eve of the Binding Festival—in six days. He offers his help knowing it means excommunication or death. Emotional beat: choosing a side.

chapters.title: Pip's Song
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip reveals the map isn't directions—it's a key that must be sung, and Pip has been learning it in dreams. But each verse Pip sings, something answers from under the harbor. Emotional beat: innocence entangled in dread.

chapters.title: The Veil Offers
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In a dream, the Veil speaks directly: it offers to restore the swordspeakers, return Ulyana's master, unmake his exile—if he simply stops. It shows him visions of the peace his silence bought. Emotional beat: temptation wearing love's face.

chapters.title: What Silence Bought
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Ulyana nearly accepts; Ines finds him packing to leave. She tells him hiding didn't save anyone—it just meant no one was there when her brother needed one. Ulyana burns his false identity papers. Emotional beat: the turning point.

chapters.title: Storming the Festival
chapters.summary: Shared POV. The Binding Festival begins; the Veil plans to renew the king's binding for another century using harvested children—including Pip, taken by inquisitors. The group splits: Cassian causes a diversion, Ines goes for Pip, Ulyana descends toward the cathedral. Emotional beat: desperate momentum.

chapters.title: Beneath the Palace
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The drowned cathedral, airless and lit by the Veil's glow. Ulyana finds his master's skeleton still kneeling at the altar—she never fled; she stayed to hold the seal as long as she could. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The Veil offers its final bargain: Ulyana's voice and magic in exchange for the king's freedom. Above, Ines fights to reach Pip; Cassian falls holding the door. Ulyana speaks the unbinding in swordspeech, feeling the words tear out of him forever. Emotional beat: sacrifice without hesitation.

chapters.title: The King Remembers
chapters.summary: King Aldric's POV. Freed after decades, the true king surfaces in his own body, remembering everything the Veil did through him. He orders the inquisitors stood down and kneels to Ulyana, who can no longer speak magic—or much of anything above a whisper. Emotional beat: hollow victory, real justice.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The city reels; magic is debated openly for the first time in years. Ines buries her brother properly, with Pip and a hoarse-voiced Ulyana beside her. Cassian survives, excommunicated and lighter for it. Emotional beat: mourning and mending intertwined.

chapters.title: A Shop with New Signs
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Months later, Ulyana reopens the charm shop—not hiding now, though the charms are only charms. Pip studies under the rebuilt order's few survivors; Ines runs routes that carry letters instead of secrets. Emotional beat: quiet joy earned.

chapters.title: The Last Oath
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the restored cathedral, Ulyana swears a new oath aloud—one with no magic in it, only words: to be present, to be found, to stay. His found family stands witness. The map, its song finished, finally goes silent. Emotional beat: homecoming; the theme resolved—power lost, family gained.
